==Problem==
The land of Catania uses gold coins and silver coins. Gold coins are <imath>1</imath> mm thick and silver coins are <imath>3</imath> mm thick. In how many ways can Taylor make a stack of coins that is <imath>8</imath> mm tall using any arrangement of gold and silver coins, assuming order matters?

<imath>\textbf{(A) }3\qquad\textbf{(B) }7\qquad\textbf{(C) }10\qquad\textbf{(D) }13\qquad\textbf{(E) }16</imath>

==Solution 1==

A stack containing <imath>3</imath> or more silver coins is at least <imath>9</imath> mm tall, so a stack of height <imath>8</imath> mm may contain at most <imath>2</imath> silver coins.

An <imath>8</imath> mm stack with <imath>0</imath> silver coins contains <imath>8</imath> gold coins.  There is <imath>\binom{8}{0} = 1</imath> such stack.

An <imath>8</imath> mm stack with <imath>1</imath> silver coin contains <imath>5</imath> gold coins.  There are <imath>\binom{6}{1} = 6</imath> such stacks.

An <imath>8</imath> mm stack with <imath>2</imath> silver coins contains <imath>2</imath> gold coins.  There are <imath>\binom{4}{2} = 6</imath> such stacks.

Thus there are <imath>1+6+6=\boxed{\textbf{(D)}\ 13}</imath> different <imath>8</imath> mm stacks.  

~Baihly2024, Pinotation, Pillowwillowtree01, edited by j314andrews, edited by kirigami789

==Solution 2 (Recursion)==

Let <imath>a_k</imath> be the number of different stacks of height <imath>k</imath> mm.  Then <imath>a_1 = 1</imath>, as the only possible <imath>1</imath> mm stack is a single gold coin.  Also <imath>a_2 = 1</imath>, as the only possible <imath>2</imath> mm stack is two gold coins, while <imath>a_3 = 2</imath>, as the two possible <imath>3</imath> mm stacks are either three gold coins or one silver coin.

If <imath>k \geq 4</imath>, a stack of height <imath>k</imath> mm can be formed by placing a stack of height <imath>(k - 1)</imath> mm on a gold coin or placing a stack of height <imath>(k - 3)</imath> mm on a silver coin.  Therefore, <imath>a_k = a_{k-1} + a_{k-3}</imath>.  So <imath>a_4 = 3</imath>, <imath>a_5 = 4</imath>, <imath>a_6 = 6</imath>, <imath>a_7 = 9</imath>, and <imath>a_8 = \boxed{\textbf{(D)}\ 13}</imath>.

-j314andrews
